source_text: Ἐπεὶ (δὲ) περὶ τηλικούτων ἐξετάζοντες πραγμάτων, οὐχ ἀρχούμενοι ταῖς κοιναῖς ἐνγοίαις καὶ τῇ ἐναργείᾳ τῶν βλεπομένων, προσπαραλαμβάνομεν εἰς τὴν φαινομένην ἡμῖν ἀπόδειξιν τῶν λεγομένων μαρτύρια τὰ ἐκ τῶν πεπιστευμένων ἡμῖν εἶναι ϑείων γραφῶν, τῆς τε λεγομένης παλαιᾶς διαϑήκης καὶ τῆς καλουμένης καινῆς, λόγῳ τε πειρώμεθα χρατύνειν ἡμῶν τὴν πίστιν, καὶ οὐδέπω περὶ τῶν γραφῶν ὡς ϑείων διελέχϑημεν᾽ φέρε καὶ περὶ τούτων ὀλίγα ὡς ἐν ἐπιτομῇ διαλάβωμεν, τὰ κινοῦντα ἡμᾶς Oc περὶ ϑείων γραμμάτων εἰς τοῦτο παρατιϑέμενοι. καὶ πρῶτόν γε, (πρὸ) τοῦ ar αὐτῶν τῶν γραμμάτων xoi τῶν ἐν αὐτοῖς δηλουμένων ῥητοῖς χρήσασϑαι, περὶ Μωσέως καὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, τοῦ νομοϑέτου τῶν Ἑβραίων καὶ τοῦ εἰσηγητοῦ τῶν χατὰ χριστιανισμὸν σωτηρίων δογμάτων, ταῦτα διαληπτέον. Πλείστων γὰρ ὅσων νομοϑετῶν γεγενημένων ἐν “Πλλησι καὶ βαρ- 10 βάροις, καὶ διδασκάλων δόγματα καταγγελλόντων ἐπαγγελλόμενα τὴν ἀλήϑειαν, οὐδένα ἱστορήσαμεν νομοϑέτην ζῆλον ἐμποιῆσαι δεδυνημένον τοῖς λοιποῖς ἔϑνεσι περὶ τοῦ παραδέξασϑαι τοὺς λόγους αὐτοῦ" πολλήν τε παρασκευὴν τὴν μετὰ τῆς δοκούσης ἀποδείξεως λογικῆς εἰσενεγκαμένων τῶν περὶ ἀληϑείας φιλοσοφεῖν ἐπαγγελλομένων, οὐδεὶς δεδύνηται τὴν νομισϑεῖσαν αὐτῷ ἀλήϑειαν ἔϑνεσι διαφόροις ἐμποιῆςσαι, ἢ ἕνὸς ἔϑνους ἀξιολόγοις πλήϑεσι. καίτοιγε ἐβούλοντο ἂν καὶ οἱ νομοϑέται χρατῦναι τοὺς φανέντας νόμους εἶναι καλοὺς εἰ δυνατὸν παρὰ παντὶ τῷ τῶν ἀνϑρώποων γένει, οἵ τε διδάσκαλοι ἐπινεμηϑῆναι ἢ“ ἐφαντάσϑησαν εἶναι ἀλήϑειαν πανταχοῦ τῆς οἰχουμένης. ἀλλ᾽ ὡς οὐ δυνάμενοι προσκαλέσασϑαι τοὺς ἀπὸ τῶν ἑτέρων διαλέχτων καὶ τῶν πολλῶν ἐϑνῶν ἐπὶ τὴν τήρησιν τῶν νόμων καὶ τὴν“ παραδοχὴν τῶν μαϑημάτων, τοῦτο ποιῆσαι οὐδὲ ἐπεβάλοντο τὴν ἀρχήν, οὐκ ἀφρόνως γε σκοπήσαντες περὶ τοῦ ἀδύνατον αὐτοῖς τὸ τοιοῦτον τυγχάνειν. πᾶσα δὲ Ἑλλὰς καὶ βάρβαρος ἡ κατὰ τὴν οἰχουμένην ἡμῶν ζηλωτὰς ἔχει μυρίους, καταλιπόντας τοὺς πατρῴους νόμους καὶ νομιζομένους ϑεούς, τῆς τηρήσεως τῶν δὶιωσέως νόμων καὶ τῆς μαϑητείας τῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ λόγων" καίτοιγε μισουμένων μὲν ὑπὸ τῶν τὰ ἀγάλματα προσχυνούντων τῶν τῷ Moofoc νόμῳ προστιϑεμένων, καὶ τὴν ἐπὶ ϑανάτῳ δὲ πρὸς τῷ μισεῖσϑαι κινδυνευόντων τῶν τὸν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ λόγον παραδεξαμένων.
pass_a_gloss: Since we are examining such great matters, not being led by common opinions and the clearness of things seen, we take as additional evidence for the apparent proof of the things being said the testimonies from the writings believed by us to be divine, both the so-called old covenant and the new covenant, and we try to strengthen our faith with reason, and we have not yet discussed the writings as divine; come, let us take up a few things about these in brief, the things moving us concerning divine writings, setting them forth for this purpose. And first, before using the writings themselves and the statements in them, we must understand the things about Moses and Jesus Christ, the lawgiver of the Hebrews and the introducer of the saving doctrines according to Christianity. For most of the lawgivers who have come to be among many peoples and barbarians, and teachers proclaiming doctrines promising truth, we have not found any lawgiver able to inspire zeal in the other nations to receive his words, and many have brought in a great preparation with what seems to be logical proof, promising to philosophize about truth, but no one has been able to inspire the truth believed by him in different nations or in worthy multitudes of one nation. And indeed the lawgivers wanted to, if possible, make the laws that have appeared to be good prevail among all humanity, and the teachers wanted to or seemed to be truth everywhere in the world. But since they were not able to summon those from other languages and many nations to keep the laws and receive the teachings, they did not even attempt to do this at the beginning, not thoughtlessly considering the impossibility for them. But all Greece and the barbarian world in our inhabited world have countless zealots, leaving behind the ancestral laws and the gods believed in, for the keeping of the laws of Jesus Christ and the discipleship of his words, although they are hated by those who reverence idols and are added to the law of Moses, and are in danger of death because of the hatred of those who have received the word of Jesus Christ.
pass_b_english: Since we are examining matters of such magnitude, we are not guided by common opinions or by the obviousness of what is seen. Instead, we bring in as additional support for the apparent proof of what we are saying the testimonies drawn from the writings we believe to be divine — both the so-called Old Covenant and the one called the New — and we attempt to reinforce our faith by means of reason. We have not yet spoken of these writings as divine; come then, let us take up a few points about them in summary, setting forth the considerations that move us concerning divine Scripture.

First of all, before we draw on the writings themselves and the statements they contain, we must understand the figures of Moses and Jesus Christ: Moses, the lawgiver of the Hebrews, and Jesus Christ, the expounder of the saving doctrines of Christianity. For among the many lawgivers who have arisen among Greeks and barbarians, and among the many teachers who have proclaimed doctrines promising truth, we find no lawgiver who was able to kindle zeal in other nations to accept his words. Many have brought forward an elaborate preparation accompanied by what seems to be logical proof, promising to philosophize about truth; yet not one has succeeded in planting the truth he himself believed among diverse nations, or even among significant multitudes of a single nation.

And indeed the lawgivers would have wished, if it were possible, to make the laws that appeared good prevail among the whole human race, and the teachers would have wished — or at least imagined — their truth to spread everywhere in the inhabited world. But because they were unable to summon people of other languages and many nations to the observance of their laws and the acceptance of their teachings, they did not even attempt such a thing from the outset, having shrewdly recognized the impossibility of it for themselves.

Yet the whole of Greece and the barbarian world throughout our inhabited world now possess countless zealots who have abandoned their ancestral laws and the gods they once revered, devoting themselves to the observance of the laws of Jesus Christ and to discipleship to his words — even though they are hated by those who venerate idols and by those who adhere to the law of Moses, and even though they face the danger of death because of the hatred directed at those who have received the word of Jesus Christ.
